analysis:
The PR changes CI workflows, docs and a changelog only; no provider runtime, coordinator contract, attestation, key handling or prefix-cache code (T-041 files) is touched, so no threat-model asset or boundary behaviour changes.

CI hardening looks neutral or positive: checkouts add persist-credentials:false so the job token is not stored in the cached .git/config (ci.yml heads 688-691, 1027-1032). SAVE_CACHES is limited to push events on master/dev, so pull-request code cannot write cache entries that later trusted runs restore. Cache poisoning of the master/dev scope by PRs is therefore reduced. Restored .git is fsck-checked, but that checks connectivity only. A cache saved by a master/dev push is trusted by later runs; this is the same trust boundary as before. Cache keys use pinned action SHAs.

component-changes.yml adds a mimo_audio output; the classifier script (scripts/ci-component-paths.py) is not supplied, so I could not verify that it emits the output. A misclassification would only skip a MiMo audio gate on PRs, and the docs say it still runs on master pushes. The provider-test-gate (ci.yml 1170-1202) still requires test-provider, summary, cluster and cluster-focused results, but the MiMo audio job does not appear in this excerpt, so gate coverage for it is unverified.

docs-impact.yml uses a blobless, sparse checkout of the PR head SHA. The workflow has contents:read only and runs scripts from the checked-out PR head; that is pre-existing. The sparse exclusion could in principle hide files from the docs check, but the docs say evidence tarballs are never read.

Unverified contracts: the Darkbloom routing plane (branch_not_admitted behaviour for push events), install-release-cmake.sh tool-cache reuse (the docs say it verifies the version, not a checksum, when reusing the image's CMake) and the provider-ci-build composite action were not supplied. Supply-chain trust for a pre-installed CMake in the runner image falls outside the supplied evidence. No finding qualifies.
